verdict: It would produce a handsome, well-timed minute with one image people remember, and I would watch episode one, but for the wrong reason: I would think it was about a ferry crew and a giant robot. Of the five things a newcomer needs, only "who these people are" is on screen (name cards, places, props). That a lamp burns because someone is watching it, that the pale figures are the dead, what Continuity sells, and whose machine No. 4 is and what cutting its cable does are all assumed from the bible. The six fixes are small, stay inside the puppet vocabulary and move no music sync point (they add two accents and move one cut by a beat); nothing is animated and no theme exists yet, so they are free now.
strongest: A window opening in the chest of the only figure built without one (f2_window, 52.0 s, on the half-time). It is the one place where the design rule (everyone is a dark shape with one lit window) becomes an event, and it rhymes with the cold open, where four windows are punched into the black before there are any figures. As boarded, the image I would remember from one viewing is its set-up, the break at 32 s (black, silence, an eye, then the tilt up No. 4 with the ferry at its shin); the window itself is the least prepared beat in the minute, which is why it is must-fix 1.

verdict: In outline yes, as boarded not yet. The skeleton is right for a TV opening (a count-in cold open, the title at 4 s, a break and reveal into the chorus, a half-time breath before the group shot), and the lit-window motif gives it an identity. But 8-24 s will play as a slideshow of four identical 4-second cards, the chorus peaks on objects instead of people, and both the best idea (No. 4's window) and the final image are staged so that they cannot land. Every fix below uses only what the kit already does; I test-rendered the proposed cut-in framings and end card through common.py to check the numbers (scratch only, no project files touched).
strongest: f2_window: a window opening in the chest of the only figure that has none. It answers the cold open, where four windows snap on in the dark before the people around them are visible. The cold open's count-in (two blinks, four punches, hit) is the best-boarded passage; the window is the best idea and the one worth rewatching for, once the viewer can tell whose chest it is.

verdict: Yes: the shape is right and the grid is clean. I checked every pose, second and bar in the unit table, the storyboard and the sync list against each other and found no arithmetic errors (720 poses; every listed accent lands where the list says). The music plan is sound: all accents sit on quarter-note beats (Dee's punches on the backbeat, the snap on the pickup into the walk, the button on the downbeat of bar 30), the form is a regular 2 + 2 + 8 + 4, a one-bar break, an 8-bar chorus and 4 bars of half-time, and a full bar of black and silence split by the eye on beat 3 is long enough to register. What will go wrong is in what the grid leaves unsaid, and I confirmed each by running the kit in memory (no project file was edited): the closing image exists for one pose and the build cuts the ring-out off; the montage and the four-person walk ask for things that cannot be read or cannot be done as written; No. 4's face arrives between beats with about a second to live; and several gestures and name cards do not read in a dark-on-dark vocabulary. All six are cheap to fix in the brief now.
strongest: a_open, poses 24-48: four ticket punches on the four beats of bar 2, each switching on one window in the dark, then the title hit showing the people standing round them. In four seconds and without a word it teaches the design language (a person is a lit window), the sound of the world (the punch is the percussion) and the sync contract; h_lineup pays it back as the ending.
